cover.benefit: Venfour helps a client understand the insurer's vehicle value, organize relevant evidence and ask clear questions. The client receives a shareable review, a prepared reconsideration request when supported, and guidance on the insurer's reply.
cover.workflow_note: A challenge is prepared when the completed review supports one.
cover.case_line: 80,000 miles / Chicago area, ZIP 60618 / Loss: September 2, 2026
cover.case_meta: Jordan Lee / Sample Insurer / Review: September 18, 2026
cover.conclusion: Here, the insurer's $20,500 value is below all five asking prices, and a repeated condition deduction is unexplained. The evidence supports asking for reconsideration.
cover.gap_note: The $2,400 difference is an asking-price comparison, not a proven valuation error or recoverable amount. The evidence and calculations follow on pages 2-3.
cover.sample_note: All case data, records, listings, correspondence and outcomes are hypothetical. No real claim or live listings were used. This combined demonstration packet illustrates the review and related guidance; it is not an exact application export.

insurer_review.intro: The hypothetical September 8 report (R1) values the vehicle at $20,500. Venfour reviews its vehicle details, comparable vehicles and disclosed adjustments alongside customer information and separate market evidence.
insurer_review.scope: Subject: 2020 Toyota RAV4 XLE AWD, 80,000 miles. The customer reports normal pre-loss condition, no existing damage and standard XLE equipment. These facts are customer-reported; no physical inspection was performed.
insurer_review.table_note: All three insurer comparables are 2020 RAV4 XLE AWD vehicles. Hypothetical USD amounts; other disclosed adjustments are $0. These are the insurer's adjustments, not independent Venfour adjustments.
findings: The report gives no itemized basis for the same deduction on all three vehicles. Ask what it represents and what evidence supports it. Repetition alone does not establish an error.
The insurer subtracts for lower-mileage vehicles and adds for a higher-mileage vehicle. Ask how the amounts were determined; the report does not explain the method.
Market evidence: a difference worth explaining
All five asking prices on page 3 exceed the insurer's value. Ask the adjuster to address those records and any differences that affect the comparison.
insurer_review.action: Request the basis for the deductions and an updated valuation report or written explanation. Do not add $1,100 to the $2,400 asking-price gap: they examine the same valuation and may overlap.

market_review.intro: Five separate hypothetical 2020 Toyota RAV4 XLE AWD vehicles match the subject. All five are assumed advertised on September 2 for illustration; no historical records were actually retrieved.
market_review.table_note: Distances are hypothetical miles from ZIP 60618. Sample IDs replace identifying VINs and listing details; there are no live listing links.
market_review.chart_note: The median gap is $22,900 - $20,500 = $2,400 (11.7%). The gap to the lowest asking price is $1,900. These comparisons support a review question, not a new appraised value or a promised increase.
market_review.selection: The complete sample set excludes duplicates and the subject vehicle. Venfour ranks by similarity, not price. Current listings cannot verify loss-date prices.
market_review.limits: Asking prices are not verified sales. No independent dollar adjustments for mileage, condition, equipment, location, certification or warranty. Condition and equipment may differ; this set is not the entire market.

request.intro: The client reviews the facts, recipient and attachments, then sends the request through their own email or insurer channel. This ready-to-send wording is for the hypothetical case only.
request.subject: Request to review vehicle valuation - claim SAMPLE-TL-2026-01
paragraphs: Thank you for your help with my total-loss claim for my 2020 Toyota RAV4 XLE AWD. I reviewed the September 8 report and would appreciate another look at the $20,500 vehicle valuation.

The attached review includes five comparable vehicles with asking prices from $22,400 to $23,400 and a median of $22,900. The records relate to the September 2 loss date. I understand these are asking prices rather than verified sale prices, and vehicle differences may affect the comparison.

Could you please explain the $1,100 condition deduction applied to each comparable and the evidence supporting it? I reported normal pre-loss condition and no existing damage. I would also appreciate an explanation of the mileage adjustments.

Please reconsider the vehicle valuation in light of these records. If it remains unchanged, could you explain how the comparable vehicles were considered and which differences or adjustments support the result? An updated valuation report or written explanation would be helpful.

Thank you for your time and help,
Jordan Lee
request.after: Attach the actual case review and supporting evidence, send the request, and mark it as sent in Venfour. Keep the sent copy. When the insurer replies, paste its response or upload the original and record any revised vehicle-value amount.
request.sample_note: Never submit this sample packet or its invented records as evidence for a real claim.

response.intro: In this hypothetical continuation, the client saves the written reply and revised report with the original request and evidence. The original review supports continuation; the new reply and amount are readable and consistent.
response.reply: We revised the vehicle valuation to $21,300. The condition deduction is now $300 per comparable; other adjustments and weighting are unchanged. The condition adjustment reflects wear.
response.report_note: Revised report R2: I1 $21,300; I2 $21,700; I3 $20,900. Equal-weight mean: $21,300. These reproduce the insurer's revised figures; the original Venfour review is unchanged.
response.addressed: Addressed: the insurer reduces the condition deduction. Unresolved: the remaining $300 deduction, mileage method and treatment of the five market records still lack a specific explanation.
response.action: Supported next action: ask for the adjustment basis. The customer chooses to continue and prepares a follow-up using the saved evidence. This clarification does not amount to a recommendation to reject $21,300; the product has no clear accept-or-reject recommendation on this revised offer.
response.subject: Follow-up on vehicle valuation - claim SAMPLE-TL-2026-01
paragraphs: Thank you for the revised report. I understand the vehicle valuation is $21,300.
You noted that the condition adjustment reflects wear. Could you please explain how the remaining condition and mileage adjustments were determined and how they apply to my vehicle?
I've attached the review again. Please reconsider the valuation in light of this evidence and send any updated report. If it remains unchanged, a brief explanation would help me understand.

Thank you for your help,
Jordan Lee
response.send_note: Customer-reviewed example of a supported follow-up. The client sends it, marks it as sent and adds any later reply to the case. No final outcome is assumed.

handoff.intro: The client works directly with Venfour on the vehicle-valuation review. You can share the customer-start link below; the client submits their insurer report and follows the guided process.
handoff.benefit: The report, evidence and prepared correspondence give the client a structured way to raise the property-damage valuation question. Counsel can review one organized record rather than assemble it from scattered documents.
steps: Venfour reviews the supplied valuation and organizes its findings and comparable evidence in a downloadable report.
When supported, the client receives a prepared request and guidance after sharing the insurer's reply. Follow-up preparation depends on the saved evidence and the client's choice to continue.
The client reviews and sends insurer communications. Venfour does not negotiate directly with the carrier or accept an offer on the client's behalf.
handoff.price_note: No subscription. The customer starts with a free valuation and can proceed to the paid full review. A higher vehicle valuation or settlement is not guaranteed.
refunds: 1. No supported dispute: automatic full refund

If the completed review does not reasonably support a dispute, the full fee is refunded automatically. The client keeps access to the completed review and report; no insurer request or final reply is required.

After sending the Venfour-supported request and evidence and following the process, the client may request a full refund if the final verified vehicle-value increase is less than $1,000. Provide final-outcome documentation and apply within 30 days of the insurer's final written response.
handoff.refund_note: The threshold compares final vehicle value with the value at purchase, not the settlement check. An interim reply is not a final outcome; exactly $1,000 does not qualify for the manual path.
handoff.cta: Share this link with your client
handoff.limits: Evidence review, not legal advice, an independent appraisal or a determination of what is owed. Taxes, fees, deductible, loan payoff and other settlement items are outside this sample's vehicle-value comparison.
